sre-bot: ALERT: GPU pool 'hotpath-primary' queue depth > 95% for 3m, throttle rate increasing, autoscaler attempted 3x and hit pool_scale_limit. Pager escalated to #incidents :rotating_light:
sre-bot: metrics snapshot: cpu_util=78%, gpu_mem=98%, inflight_requests=1240, queued=980, avg_latency_p95=1.8s
ops-oncall: I'm on it. Jumping into the autoscaler logs now.
jamie: seeing a big growth in small request bursts to the hotpath model. queue growth starts ~2026-03-15T21:09Z. any new rollouts?
margo: no manual rollout from our side. last batch/continuous-batching change merged yesterday by diego: `batchwindow=80ms -> 200ms` (intended to reduce cost). Could that slow throughput?
diego: I reverted an experiment earlier but I didn't touch hotpath. I'll pull the commit.
jamie: logs from autoscaler: ```
ERROR autoscaler: scale_attempt=3 desired=12 current=4 reason="scale_limit_reached" pool="hotpath-primary"
WARN batch_coordinator: continuous_batch_window_ms=200 (was 80) active_batches=220 batch_fill_time_ms=190
WARN kvcache: prefix_cache_miss_rate=0.42 evictions=480/s ttl_ms=60000
```
ops-oncall: prefix cache miss spike lines up with throughput drop. If batching window is larger, single-request latency may increase while tokens per batch improve — but here we see more evictions leading to wasted KV hot cache population. that reduces effective throughput.
jamie: also autoscaler reports `scale_cap=12` from committed reserved capacity, but pool has hotshard pack conflicts. infra-bot shows two hotshards pinned to the same node.
infra-bot: detected handshake failure between shard-manager and pool-provisioner: `Err: allocation_conflict: node_affinity_mismatch` for shards 7 & 9. Rebalance scheduled but stuck due to pending eviction.
margo: this looks like a config regression trio: batch window bump + prefix cache TTL change (commit f3b9) + shard affinity tweak (commit a2c1). All landed in the last 24h.
ops-oncall: immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback batchwindow to 80ms 2) increase prefix cache size/ttl 3) temporarily raise autoscaler cap 4) manual reassign hotshards. Which should we do now?
jamie: 1 and 3 quick — rollback batchwindow and bump scale cap to 20 to buy time. manual shard reassign while we rollback config.
diego: I can push the rollback PR now. PR: `revert: batchwindow change (f3b9)` — deploying to canary then hotpath.
ops-oncall: I'm going to open an emergency runbook step and run the scale override: ```
POST https://internal-api.redwood/infra/pools/hotpath-primary/override-scale
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "override_desired": 20,
  "reason": "emergency hotpath surge"
}
```
ops-oncall: executed override — response `200 OK` — autoscaler acknowledges desired=20. waiting for nodes to come up.
infra-bot: new instances provisioning in us-west-2 (3x p4d). ETA 2m.
customer-ops: @customer-ops FYI — we are seeing elevated 429s for some enterprise customers hitting hotpath. can you flag high-priority customers?
customer-ops: flagged: AcmeAnalytics, StreamlineAI, FinOpsPro — notified their CSMs and put a high-priority support banner.
margo: rollout from diego merged and canary looks green. initiating rollback to batchwindow=80ms on hotpath-primary now.
diego: rollback applied, restarting batch coordinator. logs:
```
INFO batch_coordinator: continuous_batch_window_ms=80 active_batches=90 batch_fill_time_ms=55
INFO kvcache: prefix_cache_miss_rate=0.05 evictions=12/s ttl_ms=60000
```
jamie: prefix cache miss rate dropped to normal. queue depth falling: queued=220 inflight=680. p95 latency -> 1.0s.
ops-oncall: autoscaler override still in place; nodes are healthy. I'm going to remove the override after we confirm steady state to let autoscaler manage.
ops-oncall: removing override now. ``DELETE /infra/pools/hotpath-primary/override-scale`` -> `200 OK`
infra-bot: rebalancer completed shard moves; hotshards distributed across nodes.
margo: live mitigation summary: rolled back batchwindow, temporarily raised desired capacity to 20 then removed override, manual shard rebalance completed, prefix cache behavior restored.
jamie: customer impact: transient 5-15% 429s and elevated latency for 45m window. Affected customers listed above; no data loss.
customer-ops: note: AcmeAnalytics reported 6 timeouts; CSM reached out and offered a 1-day credit proactively.
ops-oncall: incident -> mitigated. I'll keep monitoring for 2 hours then create incident timeline + postmortem. tagging @margo for ownership of postmortem. :white_check_mark:
margo: taking postmortem. action items I already note: 1) Add a CI gate to block simultaneous batching + prefixcache + shard-affinity changes 2) Add alert: prefix_cache_miss_rate > 0.2 with autoscaler_scale_failures > 1 3) Add a playbook entry to prefer scale override only after quick rollback attempt.
diego: I'll revert the shard-affinity tweak and open a follow-up to test interactions.
sre-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: hotpath-primary queue under threshold for 10m, final metrics: queued=18, inflight=210, p95=0.98s.
ops-oncall: last note — we should run a canary that simulates small-burst patterns against batchwindow=200ms next week rather than rolling to hotpath without load testing.
jamie: agreed. closing thread but will attach logs and commands to the PM doc.
margo: +1. thanks everyone for fast ops. :hands_together:
